The reported uncertainty intervals (e.g., 95% confidence intervals) and comparisons across countries imply that the OECD’s standard complex-survey estimation procedures were applied in the database tables cited (e.g., I.B1.* and II.B1.*). The note also highlights that non-response and non-participation can bias mean scores upward slightly, especially for trend comparisons, indicating that non-response adjustments/diagnostics were part of the standard PISA reporting workflow even though the specific weighting variables are not shown here.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 United Kingdom factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed relative to earlier cycles (notably 2018 and 2012). It reports mean performance trends, proficiency distributions (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6), and gaps by socio-economic status (ESCS quintiles), gender, and immigrant background, alongside contextual indicators such as belonging, discipline in mathematics lessons, safety, parental involvement, and experiences during COVID-related closures. For the United Kingdom, 12,972 students in 451 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading, or science, representing about 97% of the 15-year-old population. The note cautions that response and participation rates fell below PISA technical standards in 2022, implying that reported mean scores may be slightly higher than hypothetical means including non-respondents, with trend bias potentially smaller or absent. No machine-learning models are trained or evaluated in this document; it is a descriptive reporting of OECD’s scaled PISA results and benchmarks.
